question: How do traditional inheritance customs keep the strong preference for male children alive?

options.A: By forbidding males from owning property outside their hometown
options.B: By preventing female children from inheriting family land and property
options.C: By requiring daughters to pay a special tax to the family head
options.D: By granting double inheritance shares exclusively to first-born girls

explanation: When daughters are blocked from inheriting land or family property, families feel forced to push for a son so their property stays protected. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T8#GNS225_U6_T8_h2)

question: A newly diagnosed patient wants to start ARVs right away, but tests show they have active meningitis. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Switch the patient to herbal remedies instead of modern drugs
options.B: Refuse to give any counseling because the patient is too sick
options.C: Start the medication immediately without waiting for any other tests
options.D: Support delaying ART briefly while the acute meningitis is treated

explanation: Correct! For serious infections like meningitis, doctors treat the acute infection first before starting ART to prevent dangerous inflammation reactions in the immune system. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h5)

question: What makes a portal system different from normal blood circulation?

options.A: It carries oxygenated blood directly from the lungs to the brain
options.B: It pumps blood directly from veins into arteries without using capillaries
options.C: It connects two capillary beds through a vein before returning to the heart
options.D: It bypasses the heart completely using specialized lymphatic vessels

explanation: Think of a portal system as a special detour! Instead of going straight back to the heart, blood flows through one capillary bed, travels through a vein, and hits a second capillary bed first. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h1)

question: When should discharge planning ideally begin in a rehabilitation hospital?

options.A: Only after the final therapy session is completed
options.B: Twenty-four hours before the patient leaves
options.C: When the insurance company stops paying for care
options.D: The moment the patient is admitted to the facility

explanation: Spot on! Starting discharge planning early ensures that home equipment, family training, and support services are ready without a last-minute rush. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h7)

question: Why do doctors often combine NK1 blockers and steroids with 5-HT3 drugs for patients on strong chemotherapy?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for intravenous fluid replacement
options.B: They prevent hair loss caused by aggressive cytotoxic medications
options.C: They neutralize the chemotherapy drugs before they damage the stomach
options.D: They target multiple distinct pathways to prevent both acute and delayed nausea

explanation: You nailed it! Hitting different receptors at the same time gives the best defense against tough, multi-day chemotherapy nausea. Teamwork in pharmacology! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h5)

question: A patient with an enlarged prostate hasn't peed in eight hours and has severe lower belly pain. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink more water to flush the system
options.B: Administer a mild oral water pill (diuretic)
options.C: Prepare equipment for urinary catheterisation as ordered
options.D: Apply a warm compress to the lower back and wait two hours

explanation: Great thinking! When urine gets trapped because of an enlarged prostate, getting it out with a catheter right away relieves the painful pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h4)

question: Why is using real data better than relying only on gut feeling during quality improvement?

options.A: Data processing is legally mandated for every single patient interaction
options.B: Data completely eliminates the need for experienced clinical staff
options.C: Data analysis is always faster than talking to patients on the ward
options.D: Data provides an objective factual reality and avoids personal bias

explanation: Our gut feelings can sometimes trick us or be biased. Clear data gives us the honest, unvarnished truth about what is happening in patient care! [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which brain structure inside the temporal lobe is vital for forming new memories?

options.A: Insula
options.B: Motor strip
options.C: Broca's area
options.D: Hippocampus

explanation: The hippocampus acts as the brain's filing system for converting short-term memories into permanent long-term storage. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h4)

question: What is the main focus of qualitative research?

options.A: Exact numerical measurements and statistics
options.B: Calculating hospital budgets and supply costs
options.C: Laboratory experiments involving chemical compounds
options.D: Human experiences, words, and meanings

explanation: Spot on! Qualitative research looks at the rich stories, feelings, and experiences of people rather than just numbers. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T1#GNS217_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses use rating scales like the CIWA-Ar for patients going through alcohol withdrawal?

options.A: To objectively measure symptom severity and guide medication doses
options.B: To determine the exact legal penalties for public intoxication
options.C: To replace the need for physical and neurological exams
options.D: To punish the patient for failing to stop drinking

explanation: Spot on! These scales take the guesswork out of care, helping us give the right medications safely and only when the patient truly needs them. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h6)

question: What does the ethical principle of non-maleficence require of a nurse?

options.A: To let clients make every medical decision independently
options.B: To divide hospital resources equally among all available staff
options.C: To do no harm and protect the client from injury
options.D: To always tell the absolute truth regardless of consequences

explanation: Non-maleficence is the core professional duty to avoid inflicting physical or emotional harm on the client. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h2)

question: A young child comes in with frequent diarrhea, slow growth, and wounds that take too long to heal. Which deficiency is most likely the cause?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Iron
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Zinc

explanation: Well done! Zinc is a superstar for a child's immune system, gut health, and growth. When it's low, healing and recovery slow down. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why do theatres carefully monitor room temperature and humidity during surgery?

options.A: To make the room comfortable for visitors and family members
options.B: To ensure surgical instruments do not rust during the procedure
options.C: To discourage bacterial growth and prevent patient hypothermia
options.D: To keep the anesthesia machine running at peak efficiency

explanation: Controlling the climate stops bacteria from multiplying and protects the patient's body heat while they are under anesthesia. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h1)

question: A patient wakes up gasping for air two hours after falling asleep and has to sit by the window to breathe. What is this called?

options.A: Acute bronchial asthma
options.B: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
options.C: Simple sleep apnea
options.D: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

explanation: You're doing great! Waking up suddenly in the middle of the night feeling starved for air is known as paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (PND). It's a classic sign often seen in heart issues. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h2)

question: Blood is soaking right through the gauze on a leg wound you are pressing. What should you do next?

options.A: Remove the soaked gauze to inspect the cut
options.B: Stop pressing entirely and prep for surgery
options.C: Rinse the wound with sterile saline
options.D: Add more gauze pads right on top of the old ones and keep pressing

explanation: Never take off the first layer of gauze—you'll tear away the tiny new clots trying to form. Just pile more on top and keep holding pressure! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why do patients with vulvitis often feel a burning sensation when passing urine?

options.A: The urethral opening becomes completely blocked by swelling.
options.B: Urine flows over raw, inflamed skin tissues on the vulva.
options.C: The kidneys produce acidic waste products that burn the bladder.
options.D: Urine mixes directly with digestive enzymes in the pelvis.

explanation: Imagine pouring liquid over a fresh scrape—when urine washes across sensitive, raw, or inflamed vulval skin, it naturally stings. Such a logical clinical connection to remember! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h3)

question: A patient gets an allergic rash after taking a small antibiotic pill that binds to their blood proteins. What do we call this type of drug molecule?

options.A: T-independent antigen
options.B: Hapten
options.C: Superantigen
options.D: Autoantigen

explanation: Spot on! The small drug acts as a hapten, attaching to bigger body proteins and tricking the immune system into an allergic reaction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why does most of a baby's blood skip the lungs before birth?

options.A: Foetal lung tissue requires very little blood to survive and grow
options.B: The pulmonary arteries are completely blocked by scar tissue
options.C: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not yet oxygenate blood
options.D: Blood pressure in the left ventricle is much higher than the right

explanation: You've got this! Since the baby gets all its oxygen from mum through the placenta, the lungs are resting and filled with fluid. So, the body naturally diverts blood away from them. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h1)

question: What kind of genetic inheritance pattern does sickle cell anaemia follow?

options.A: Autosomal dominant
options.B: Autosomal recessive
options.C: X-linked dominant
options.D: Mitochondrial inheritance

explanation: It's autosomal recessive! This means a child needs to inherit two faulty genes—one from each parent—to actually have the disease. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is a key nursing action immediately following an ophthalmoscopy exam where dilating drops were used?

options.A: Instructing the patient to lie flat in bed for at least two hours
options.B: Checking the patient's blood pressure every five minutes for an hour
options.C: Flushing the patient's eyes with sterile saline until the pupils shrink
options.D: Ensuring the patient has safe transportation home due to blurred vision

explanation: Because dilating drops impair near vision and cause glare, patient safety requires confirming they have a ride home before leaving. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h9)

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator when a patient cannot breathe well on their own?

options.A: To deliver oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
options.B: To keep the patient completely sedated
options.C: To permanently replace natural breathing
options.D: To cure the underlying lung disease

explanation: Think of the ventilator as a helpful partner. It steps in to help with gas exchange—bringing in fresh oxygen and blowing off waste carbon dioxide—until the lungs are strong enough to take over. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T10#GNS321_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why is it helpful to have colleagues review your research report before submitting it?

options.A: Colleagues can catch errors and blind spots that the author missed
options.B: It guarantees that the research paper will win academic awards
options.C: It allows someone else to take full credit for the study
options.D: It eliminates the need for any references or citations

explanation: When you stare at your own writing for hours, you miss tiny mistakes. Fresh eyes help spot typos and confusing parts! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h10)

question: Which of these counts as a biological water pollutant?

options.A: Pathogenic bacteria and viruses
options.B: Heavy metals like mercury
options.C: Dissolved industrial solvents
options.D: Discarded plastic containers

explanation: Great job! Biological pollutants are living germs or microorganisms, often introduced into water through waste contamination. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h2)

question: Which household item is a very common fall hazard for an elderly home care patient?

options.A: Bright overhead lighting in the main hallway
options.B: Loose scatter rugs on polished wooden floors
options.C: Sturdy wooden handrails installed along a staircase
options.D: A heavy armchair placed firmly against a corner wall

explanation: Spot on! Those pretty little scatter rugs love to slide underfoot or catch walking aids like canes. Removing them is an easy win for home safety. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which problem is most linked to using steroid eye drops for a very long time?

options.A: Severe dryness and painful ulcers
options.B: Secondary glaucoma and increased eye pressure
options.C: Rapid hardening of the outer eye layer
options.D: Permanent pupil shrinkage and total blindness

explanation: Steroids are great for short-term inflammation, but long-term use can block fluid drainage and shoot pressure right up, leading to secondary glaucoma. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of cost containment in a nursing unit?

options.A: Stopping all purchases of new clinical technology permanently
options.B: Reducing unnecessary expenses without harming patient care quality
options.C: Firing experienced nurses to hire cheaper untrained workers
options.D: Cutting all spending on patient medications to maximize profit

explanation: Cost containment is about cutting waste and saving money while making sure patient safety and care quality remain top-notch. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h6)

question: What main event tells you the third stage of labour is happening?

options.A: The stabilization of maternal vital signs postpartum
options.B: Full dilation of the maternal cervix
options.C: Expulsion of the placenta and fetal membranes
options.D: The physical birth of the newborn baby

explanation: The baby is already born in stage three, so this stage is all about safely delivering the placenta. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h4)

question: What is a major goal of family planning within Primary Health Care?

options.A: Helping parents properly space their children for better health
options.B: Controlling the exact height of newborn babies
options.C: Ensuring families only have male children
options.D: Completely banning families from having children

explanation: Family planning allows mothers to regain their health between pregnancies and ensures better care for existing children. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h5)

question: What did Hippocrates mean when he famously said, 'Let food be thy medicine'?

options.A: Food has no actual impact on human health
options.B: Patients should take drugs instead of eating meals
options.C: Only doctors are allowed to prepare daily meals
options.D: Diet plays a direct role in preventing and treating illness

explanation: Spot on! Hippocrates understood early on that what we eat directly shapes our health and healing journey. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h2)

question: What does the term 'food security' refer to in nutritional nursing assessments?

options.A: Having reliable access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food
options.B: Eating only foods that have been certified organic by government agencies
options.C: Keeping hospital kitchen supplies locked away from pests
options.D: Storing perishable groceries at the correct refrigerator temperature

explanation: Food security means an individual has physical and economic access to the food they need for an active, healthy life. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h5)

question: Two clinical nurses independently score a patient's wound healing using the same chart. What type of reliability are they testing?

options.A: Parallel forms reliability
options.B: Test-retest reliability
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Internal consistency reliability

explanation: Since two separate raters are checking their agreement on the same patient, it's inter-rater reliability in action! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h5)

question: Through which part of the spinal cord do incoming sensory nerve signals enter?

options.A: Dorsal root
options.B: Lateral horn
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral root

explanation: Sensory information always comes in through the back door—the dorsal root—bringing messages from the rest of the body into the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h3)

question: Why do local rescue teams worry so much about crowd control at a disaster site?

options.A: Crowds prevent media houses from broadcasting live updates
options.B: Uncontrolled crowds often steal heavy rescue machinery
options.C: Large crowds block access roads, delay ambulances, and endanger more lives
options.D: Onlookers are required by law to assist professional paramedics

explanation: You got it! Too many curious onlookers block the roads, stopping ambulances from getting through and putting even more people in danger. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h5)

question: A senior nurse and a junior nurse keep arguing about how to dress a wound. What is this called?

options.A: Intragroup conflict
options.B: Interpersonal conflict
options.C: Organizational conflict
options.D: Intergroup conflict

explanation: When two specific people clash over methods or personalities, it's a classic interpersonal conflict. [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h3)

question: What do you call a menu that repeats itself after a set time, like every two weeks?

options.A: Static menu
options.B: Single-use menu
options.C: A la carte menu
options.D: Cycle menu

explanation: A cycle menu rotates through a set list of days, which is a lifesaver for busy hospitals and schools. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T005#GNS227_U3_T005_h4)

question: Which chart is best for tracking clinical data points over time?

options.A: Anatomical diagram
options.B: Organizational chart
options.C: Run chart
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: Think of a run chart as a story running across time. It helps us easily spot if things are going up, down, or staying steady week by week. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h4)

question: What does the important humanitarian principle of 'non-refoulement' mean?

options.A: Automatic granting of permanent citizenship in the host nation
options.B: The legal right to free higher education in the host country
options.C: Protection from being forced to return to a dangerous country
options.D: Exemption from all local taxes and immigration fees

explanation: Non-refoulement is a fancy word with a vital meaning. It simply protects refugees from being sent back to places where they face serious harm or persecution. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h1)

question: Why are nurses in a great position to spot patients who need DRF exemptions?

options.A: They make the final legal decisions on hospital budgets
options.B: They personally purchase all the drugs sold in the pharmacy
options.C: They are responsible for auditing the hospital's bank accounts
options.D: They spend the most direct time at the patient's bedside

explanation: Because nurses are constantly at the bedside, they are the first to notice when a patient is struggling to afford their prescribed medications. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h8)

question: Why is blood pressure in the pulmonary circulation much lower than in systemic circulation?

options.A: To protect delicate lung tissues and prevent fluid buildup
options.B: Because the right ventricle is much stronger than the left
options.C: To slow down red blood cells so they can produce more energy
options.D: Because the lungs require very little blood flow to survive

explanation: Lower pressure in the pulmonary circuit prevents excess fluid from leaking into the delicate air sacs of the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is a biophysiological measure?

options.A: Interview transcript text
options.B: Open-ended survey response
options.C: Blood glucose level
options.D: Patient satisfaction score

explanation: Biophysiological measures are physical or chemical checks on the body, like checking blood sugar or temperature. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of a localized wound infection that nurses look out for?

options.A: Purulent or foul-smelling drainage from the puncture
options.B: Worsening throbbing pain days after the initial event
options.C: Increasing redness and warmth around the injury site
options.D: Gradual shrinking and drying of the wound edges

explanation: Wound shrinking and drying means healing is going well! Spreading redness, foul pus, and worsening pain are the warning signs of infection. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which strategy best combines behaviorist and constructivist approaches in nursing school?

options.A: Focusing solely on the emotional well-being of students during exam weeks
options.B: Relying exclusively on silent reading assignments and standardized multiple-choice quizzes
options.C: Using skills checklists for procedural accuracy alongside simulation scenarios for clinical reasoning
options.D: Allowing students to do whatever clinical tasks they prefer without any supervision

explanation: Checklists help nail down precise steps (behaviorism), while simulation scenarios let you problem-solve and build deep understanding (constructivism). Perfect combo! [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h8)

question: What is NOT a typical challenge faced by disease surveillance systems in developing settings?

options.A: Delays in transporting clinical samples due to poor roads
options.B: An overabundance of fully staffed reference laboratories
options.C: Inadequate funding for rapid response outbreak teams
options.D: Poor reporting compliance by overburdened health workers

explanation: A lack of laboratories and equipment is a major challenge, not an overabundance of them. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: Why are health programs more successful when the community helps design them?

options.A: It guarantees that government funding will double
options.B: Local people trust interventions they help create
options.C: It eliminates the need for any professional nurses
options.D: Foreign donors prefer funding community-built projects

explanation: When communities are involved from the start, programs align better with local realities, leading to higher trust and acceptance. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: Why do pre-existing medical conditions often get worse during pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy significantly increases the workload on the mother's heart, lungs, and kidneys
options.B: Metabolic rates drop drastically to conserve energy for the developing baby
options.C: Hormonal surges permanently deactivate prescribed medications in the bloodstream
options.D: The growing fetus directly consumes all of the mother's circulating red blood cells

explanation: The body experiences a massive increase in blood volume and cardiac output to support the baby, which puts extra stress on organs that were already struggling. You're mastering maternal physiology! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h4)

question: Which regulatory body sets the professional and legal standards for nursing practice and documentation in Nigeria?

options.A: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body empowered to regulate nursing education, practice, and professional conduct in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the purpose of an endovascular thrombectomy procedure?

options.A: Physically remove a large blood clot from a blocked cerebral artery
options.B: Surgically repair a ruptured blood vessel inside the brain
options.C: Drain excess cerebrospinal fluid from the lateral ventricles
options.D: Bypass a narrowed carotid artery using a synthetic graft

explanation: Spot on! During a thrombectomy, doctors use specialized tools threaded through blood vessels to physically grab and pull out large clots. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why is it important to gather all your IV equipment before you walk to the patient's bedside?

options.A: It prevents the patient from feeling any pain
options.B: It ensures an efficient and organized procedure
options.C: It guarantees the vein will not rupture
options.D: It eliminates the need to wear gloves

explanation: Being prepared keeps you calm, maintains clean technique, and helps the patient feel safe and relaxed while you work. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which finding is most commonly auscultated in the lungs of a patient experiencing fluid overload?

options.A: High-pitched whistling wheezes
options.B: Absent breath sounds on the left
options.C: A loud friction rub over the trachea
options.D: Fine crackles at the lung bases

explanation: Fluid backing up into the tiny air sacs of the lungs creates a crackling sound when air pops them open during inhalation. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h5)

question: Where is sodium mostly found in the body, making it a key electrolyte?

options.A: Neutral protein molecule
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamin
options.C: Intracellular fluid (inside cells)
options.D: Extracellular fluid (outside cells)

explanation: You've got this! Sodium is a positively charged ion that stays mostly in the fluid outside of our cells, which is why it's called an extracellular cation. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h2)

question: Why does leadership matter for every nurse, even those without a fancy management title?

options.A: Staff nurses are solely responsible for hospital budgeting
options.B: Formal titles are required before a nurse can influence safety
options.C: All nurses must eventually manage a hospital department
options.D: Bedside nurses routinely guide peers and advocate for safe care

explanation: Leadership isn't just about titles! Even as a student or bedside nurse, you lead whenever you guide a colleague or speak up for your patient. [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h1)

question: What do we mean by "abnormal illness behaviour"?

options.A: Seeking help immediately after experiencing severe trauma
options.B: A response that is out of proportion to actual physical findings
options.C: Following all medical advice given by the attending nurse
options.D: Recovering from a minor illness within expected timeframes

explanation: This happens when the reaction doesn't match the medical reality—like complete denial of a serious condition, or intense panic over a tiny scratch. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T9#GNS123_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is a common emotional hurdle faced by brothers and sisters of a gifted child?

options.A: Severe physical growth delays
options.B: Automatic transfer of high intelligence
options.C: Feelings of being overshadowed or resentful
options.D: Immediate academic failure at school

explanation: It's totally natural for siblings to feel left out or pressured when all the attention at home goes toward the gifted child's achievements. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h5)

question: What does the term 'psychological safety' mean on a hospital ward?

options.A: A policy that prevents nurses from ever working night shifts
options.B: An environment where staff can speak up without fear of humiliation
options.C: A ward that has physical security guards stationed at every entrance
options.D: An agreement to never disagree with a physician's orders

explanation: Psychological safety means you can report mistakes, ask questions, and share concerns without worrying that someone will mock or punish you. [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h8)

question: Why do conditions that stop bile salt production lead to a shortage of fat-soluble vitamins?

options.A: Vitamins require acidic bile to transform into water-soluble molecules
options.B: Without bile, the stomach cannot produce enough intrinsic factor for vitamin uptake
options.C: Bile salts act as direct chemical carriers for vitamins A, D, E, and K in the blood
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins depend on lipid micelles for transport across the brush border

explanation: Spot on! Vitamins A, D, E, and K love fat, so they need bile to form tiny packages called micelles that ferry them close enough to the gut wall to be absorbed. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h5)

question: A patient is having a severe allergic reaction to a bee sting. Which antibody class is most likely elevated?

options.A: IgE
options.B: IgG
options.C: IgM
options.D: IgA

explanation: Remember: 'E' for allergy! IgE antibodies trigger mast cells to release histamine during allergic responses and when fighting off parasites. Great nursing insight! [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why do active tissues like tumors absorb large amounts of FDG during a PET scan?

options.A: Rapidly dividing cells require high amounts of energy and glucose.
options.B: Cancer cells have abnormal blood vessels that block normal water flow.
options.C: The radioactive tracer binds directly to the DNA strands of damaged cells.
options.D: Tumors actively attract and trap radioactive metal inside their walls.

explanation: Exactly! Because cancer cells grow and multiply so fast, they need a ton of energy. Since FDG acts just like glucose, the tumor sucks it right up, making it glow brightly on the scan. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h2)

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient who has recovered from serum sickness before they leave the hospital?

options.A: Demonstrate how to measure blood pressure at home twice daily
options.B: Encourage the patient to eat a high-protein diet to rebuild lost muscle
options.C: Instruct the patient to exercise their joints vigorously every single morning
options.D: Teach the patient to permanently avoid the specific triggering drug

explanation: Prevention is key! They must avoid that specific drug forever, because taking it again can cause an even faster and worse reaction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h7)

question: An elderly patient on a fixed income is skipping meals to afford prescription drugs. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Provide a strict diet chart filled with expensive organic superfoods
options.B: Connect the patient with local food assistance programs and a social worker
options.C: Advise the patient to start a vigorous workout routine to boost appetite
options.D: Tell the patient to stop buying medications and spend money only on food

explanation: Linking vulnerable patients to community resources and social workers helps fix the root cause of their food insecurity. Amazing clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT helpful to include when charting about a patient's cough?

options.C: The brand of soap used in the hospital room
options.D: Whether the cough is dry or productive

question: Why do incubatory carriers give nurses headaches when trying to stop the spread of disease?

options.A: They spread pathogens before anyone realizes they are sick
options.B: They only transmit infections through contaminated drinking water
options.C: They carry drug-resistant bacteria that resist all antibiotics
options.D: They refuse to take their prescribed medications in the ward

explanation: Since they look and feel healthy right now, nobody suspects they are passing germs around until symptoms finally show up later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h2)

question: What is a major risk if someone takes high-dose fat-soluble vitamin supplements for months without a doctor's advice?

options.A: The excess vitamins will wash out immediately in the urine.
options.B: The kidneys will stop producing urine completely within hours.
options.C: The vitamins can accumulate in body tissues to toxic levels.
options.D: The patient will instantly develop severe iron deficiency anemia.

explanation: Unlike water-soluble vitamins, fat-soluble vitamins get stored in our body fat and liver. Taking too many for too long can build up and cause toxicity! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h7)

question: Which nursing documentation detail is essential after finishing a gastric lavage session?

options.A: The brand name and factory serial number of the lavage tube
options.B: Total amounts of fluid put in and taken out of the stomach
options.C: The exact weight of the patient measured in kilograms
options.D: The name of the family member who gave consent for care

explanation: Recording fluid balance prevents water intoxication or electrolyte imbalances, confirming that the nurse recovered roughly what was instilled. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of home health care documentation?

options.A: To serve as a marketing tool for private agencies
options.B: To replace verbal reports between the nurse and family
options.C: To determine the salary of the visiting community nurse
options.D: To provide a clear clinical and legal history of care

explanation: Documentation serves as an official record of the client's status and the care provided, which is essential for clinical continuity and legal protection. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses view gender-based violence as a public health issue rather than just a private family matter?

options.A: Because hospitals are legally required to arrest the perpetrators immediately
options.B: Because the government funds all counseling services directly through health budgets
options.C: Because private family matters are completely outside the scope of nursing ethics
options.D: Because it causes widespread physical and mental harm requiring medical intervention

explanation: Spot on! Because abuse inflicts deep physical and emotional trauma on individuals and communities, nurses must treat it as a critical health priority. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h1)

question: A disease spreads rapidly across several countries and continents. What is this global event called?

options.A: Endemic
options.B: Hyperendemic
options.C: Pandemic
options.D: Holoendemic

explanation: A pandemic is an epidemic that has spread over a very wide area, crossing international borders to affect multiple countries or continents. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h2)

question: What is the main goal of a peer support program for second victims?

options.A: To find grounds for disciplinary action or termination
options.B: To re-test the nurse's clinical skills in a simulation lab
options.C: To conduct a legal investigation of the nurse's actions
options.D: To provide a confidential space to talk with trained colleagues

explanation: Sometimes you just need someone who truly understands the hospital ward stress to listen without judging. Peer support is all about healing together! [learn more](GST319_U6_T4#GST319_U6_T4_h5)

question: How soon after getting the yellow fever vaccine does protective immunity usually kick in?

options.A: After three to six weeks
options.B: Only after a second booster dose
options.C: Within ten days
options.D: Immediately within minutes

explanation: Great work! The body builds up defenses quickly, giving solid protection within about ten days of getting the jab. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h7)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for triggering the milk 'let-down' reflex when breastfeeding?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Wonderful! Oxytocin makes tiny muscles around the milk glands squeeze, pushing the milk forward for the baby. It's also the hormone of love and bonding! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h5)

question: What is the biggest danger of constant, severe scratching when a patient has a skin rash?

options.A: Triggering sudden total hair loss across the entire scalp
options.B: Permanently altering the chemical balance of natural sweat glands
options.C: Breaking the skin barrier through scratching and introducing bacterial infections
options.D: Causing the patient's blood pressure to drop rapidly into shock

explanation: Spot on! Scratching breaks open the skin's protective shield, inviting bacteria to sneak in and cause a secondary infection. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h6)

question: A pregnant client at 32 weeks gestation reports a sudden severe headache and blurred vision. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Suggest she drink more water and take a mild over-the-counter pain reliever
options.B: Notify the primary care provider immediately to evaluate for preeclampsia
options.C: Reassure her that these are normal symptoms of increased blood volume
options.D: Advise her to lie flat on her back for an hour to relieve eye strain

explanation: Severe headaches and visual disturbances are cardinal signs of gestational hypertension or preeclampsia, which require urgent medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: Why is Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) described as an ongoing cycle rather than a single event?

options.A: Because medical equipment never breaks down more than once
options.B: Because hospital management loves writing endless reports every week
options.C: Because healthcare delivery and patient needs are always changing
options.D: Because nurses have too much free time during their shifts

explanation: CQI is continuous because healthcare environments are dynamic, requiring constant monitoring and small adjustments to maintain high standards. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why do urinary buffers like phosphate and ammonia matter so much when the kidneys excrete acid?

options.A: They prevent water from being reabsorbed in the collecting duct

options.C: They supply the necessary sodium ions for the renin pathway
options.D: They bind free hydrogen ions so urine pH does not drop too low

question: How did later revisions of Nigeria's population policy change compared to the 1988 version?

options.A: They shifted toward a rights-based approach focusing on quality of life.
options.B: They focused exclusively on increasing the total population size.
options.C: They made family planning completely illegal across all states.
options.D: They abandoned all health-related goals to focus solely on taxation.

explanation: Later updates moved away from strict child limits. Instead, they focused on human rights, reproductive health, and helping families live better, sustainable lives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h1)

question: How do nurses help fulfill a hospitalized patient's need for emotional safety?

options.A: By limiting visits from family members completely
options.B: By performing procedures quickly without warning
options.C: By keeping information about treatments a secret
options.D: By explaining procedures clearly and answering questions honestly

explanation: Clear communication reduces anxiety and helps patients feel secure and in control of their situation. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: You are about to give an oral pill, but the chart says the drug should be given intravenously (IV). What do you do?

options.A: Crush the tablet and mix it with sterile water for an injection
options.B: Stop and clarify the route with the prescriber because giving drugs by the wrong route is dangerous
options.C: Give the pill by mouth anyway since the active ingredient is the same
options.D: Skip the dose completely and document that the patient refused

explanation: Route matters immensely! Changing how a drug enters the body can cause serious harm. Always pause and clarify the order if things don't match up. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T5#GNS125_U4_T5_h2)

question: A patient is scared they will suffocate when the scope goes into their nose. How should you, as the nurse, respond?

options.A: Inform them that the procedure will be canceled until their anxiety goes away completely.
options.B: Tell them to hold their breath entirely until the doctor pulls the camera back out.
options.C: Assure them that a breathing machine will completely take over their lungs during the procedure.
options.D: Explain that they will still be able to breathe freely through their nose and mouth around the thin scope.

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Reassuring patients that the scope is tiny and their airway is wide open does wonders to calm their nerves. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary definition of ambulation in healthcare?

options.A: The physical therapy exercise routine
options.B: The ability of a patient to walk
options.C: The safe transfer from bed to chair
options.D: The prevention of blood clots in legs

explanation: Ambulation simply means walking, whether done completely on one's own or with the help of a device or another person. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h1)

question: Which of these groups is considered a vulnerable population needing extra research protection?

options.A: Licensed physicians
options.B: Children
options.C: Hospital administrators
options.D: Healthy adult researchers

explanation: Correct! Children cannot give adult consent and have limited autonomy, so we must protect them extra carefully. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T19#GNS224_U1_T19_h5)

question: An emergency ward is trying out a new documentation tool. What action will best help the staff adopt it successfully?

options.A: Forcing staff to use the exact original tool without listening to their feedback
options.B: Hiding the tool instructions until every nurse has completed a written exam
options.C: Allowing the emergency nurses to adapt the tool slightly to fit their fast-paced workflow
options.D: Punishing any nurse who forgets to use the tool during the first week

explanation: Flexibility is key! When staff get to shape how a tool fits their busy shift, they feel proud and are much more likely to use it. [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h4)

question: What happens when the sleep-promoting centers quiet down the reticular activating system?

options.A: Metabolic rate spikes rapidly
options.B: Voluntary muscle tone becomes rigid
options.C: The brain transitions into sleep
options.D: Sensory awareness dramatically increases

explanation: When those wake-up signals from the reticular activating system quiet down, your brain is finally able to drift off to sleep. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h2)

question: What is the main job of Montgomery's tubercles on the areola during pregnancy and breastfeeding?

options.A: To regulate the release of prolactin from the pituitary gland

options.C: To produce the first wave of thick yellow colostrum
options.D: To secrete an oily substance that protects and lubricates the nipple

question: Which type of joint is known for having a fluid-filled space between the bones?

options.A: Fibrous joint
options.B: Suture joint
options.C: Cartilaginous joint
options.D: Synovial joint

question: Over time, how does chronic, untreated high blood pressure harm the heart?

options.A: By permanently dilating all major veins in the lower extremities
options.B: By thinning the heart muscle walls and causing extreme hypotension
options.C: By eliminating the need for peripheral vascular resistance
options.D: By injuring arterial walls and causing left ventricular hypertrophy

explanation: Fighting against high pressure everyday makes the heart muscle work out too hard—just like lifting heavy weights, it gets bulky and thick (hypertrophy), which isn't good for it long-term. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which specialist helps patients regain the ability to swallow safely?

options.A: Speech-language pathology
options.B: Occupational therapy
options.C: Respiratory therapy
options.D: Physical therapy

explanation: Spot on. Speech therapists evaluate and treat swallowing issues (dysphagia) to keep patients safe from choking or aspiration. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h3)

question: You just received a delivery of delicate protein medications for your ward. What is your very first priority?

options.A: Place the vials in a warm blanket warmer to activate them
options.B: Store them openly on the nurse's station desk for easy access
options.C: Crush the vials to prepare liquid doses for oral feeding tubes
options.D: Check and follow the required cold-chain refrigeration rules

question: Which main hormone is dangerously low during an adrenal crisis?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Vasopressin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Cortisol is our primary stress hormone. When the adrenal glands fail to pump it out, the body struggles to handle even basic stress. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h5)

question: What main substance does a Nelson inhaler deliver to help a patient breathe better?

options.A: Dry chemical powder
options.B: Medicated steam
options.C: Oxygen gas
options.D: Sterile saline mist

explanation: Spot on! The Nelson inhaler is a classic bedside tool used to vaporize hot water and soothing drugs so the patient breathes in warm, comforting medicated steam. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by nurses providing community care for special children in Nigeria?

options.C: Difficulty traveling to remote villages

question: What is the biggest danger when someone has a severe case of watery diarrhoea?

question: On a CT scan, how does dense bone usually appear?

options.A: Pitch black

question: Which two main proteins make up the tiny filaments inside a muscle sarcomere?

options.D: Myoglobin and hemoglobin

question: What is the main goal of a retrospective research study?

options.A: Testing a new drug in real time
options.B: Examining past events and records
options.C: Observing an active clinical trial
options.D: Following healthy patients for years

explanation: Great job! Think of 'retrospective' like looking in a rearview mirror—these studies look backward at data or events that already happened instead of following people forward. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T14#GNS224_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which organ failure leads directly to a dangerous buildup of water-soluble drugs in the body?

options.A: Pancreatic failure
options.B: Thyroid failure
options.C: Stomach failure
options.D: Kidney failure

explanation: Remember, the kidneys are our body's primary filtration filters for water-soluble waste and drugs. When they fail, those medications accumulate fast. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h5)

question: As a nurse, what is the main goal of gender-transformative healthcare?

options.A: To prevent teenagers from ever talking about relationships
options.B: To focus exclusively on male patients during clinic hours
options.C: To actively challenge harmful norms while improving health access
options.D: To enforce traditional cultural rules inside hospital wards

question: Why is it usually better to give pain meds on a regular schedule instead of waiting for the patient to ask?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for nursing assessments
options.B: It is cheaper for the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: It maintains a steady therapeutic level of pain relief
options.D: It stops the patient from ever sleeping deeply

explanation: Scheduled dosing keeps pain under control before it flares up, making the patient much more comfortable than a roller-coaster approach. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why should a nurse assess a patient's swallowing ability before giving oral pills?

options.B: To see if the patient has any food allergies
options.C: To check how fast the liver will metabolize the drug
options.D: To determine if the patient prefers liquid or solid medicines

explanation: Swallowing difficulties place patients at high risk of aspirating foreign objects or liquids into the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: How do health orderlies help control infections in the theatre?

options.A: They wear sterile gowns and handle surgical instruments

options.C: They help clean the theatre and dispose of waste between cases
options.D: They sterilize surgical blades inside the autoclave machine

explanation: By clearing waste and cleaning up after procedures, orderlies play a huge part in keeping the theatre safe from hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h6)

question: What are the three core components of the epidemiological triangle used in public health?

options.A: Source, vehicle, and victim

options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Reservoir, vector, and portal

question: What happens when a nursing standard is vague and unclear?

options.A: It eliminates the need for shift reports
options.B: It leads to inconsistent interpretation and varied care practices
options.C: It guarantees faster recovery times on the ward
options.D: It automatically improves patient satisfaction scores

explanation: If a rule is not clear, different nurses will interpret it in different ways, leading to uneven quality of care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the evaluation step in the nursing process?

options.A: To write a formal medical diagnosis for the physician to sign
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of hospital supplies used
options.C: To decide which nurse will work the night shift over the weekend
options.D: To determine whether established patient care goals have been successfully met

explanation: Evaluation is just checking our report card: did our nursing care help the patient reach their health goals? [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h8)

question: What do dermatophyte fungi specifically require to grow and thrive?

options.A: Peptidoglycan
options.B: Red blood cells

options.D: Oxygen

question: What is the main goal of food budgeting in clinical nutrition?

options.A: To plan food spending without compromising nutritional health
options.B: To buy only the cheapest food available on the market
options.C: To eliminate all spending on processed and convenience foods
options.D: To calculate the exact daily calorie intake of a patient

explanation: Spot on! Food budgeting is all about balancing your pocket with your plate so you never have to sacrifice good health just to save some cash. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h1)

question: Under which category of supplements is iron classified?

options.A: Enzyme
options.B: Vitamin
options.C: Mineral
options.D: Herb

explanation: Iron is a vital mineral our bodies need to build hemoglobin for red blood cells. Simple and classic nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h3)

question: Why is a physical head-to-toe check important during a nutrition assessment?

options.A: It calculates the precise daily caloric expenditure during rest
options.B: It reveals visible deficiency signs like swollen gums or pale skin
options.C: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests and dietary records
options.D: It accurately measures the exact percentage of body water volume

explanation: By simply looking at a patient's hair, skin, eyes, and mouth, you can often spot early physical clues of missing vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h7)

question: Why do anticholinergic drugs often cause annoying side effects like dry mouth and blurred vision?

options.A: They block parasympathetic nerve signals throughout the whole body
options.B: They cause a sudden drop in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: They irritate the mucous membranes in the head and neck
options.D: They dehydrate the patient by increasing kidney urine output

question: What is the primary purpose of public health surveillance systems during an infectious disease threat?

options.A: To calculate the annual financial profits of private clinics

options.C: To restrict all international trade between neighboring nations
options.D: To detect, track, and report unusual disease outbreaks quickly

question: Which skin structure produces watery fluid to help cool the body through evaporation?

options.C: Sebaceous glands

question: Why is epidemiological surveillance so important in community health?

options.A: To monitor disease trends and detect outbreaks early
options.B: To diagnose individual patients with chronic ailments
options.C: To design new pharmaceutical drugs in laboratories
options.D: To calculate monthly salaries for hospital staff members

explanation: You nailed it! Surveillance helps public health teams track disease patterns so they can catch and stop outbreaks early. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h6)

question: How much water is normally used to flush a nasogastric tube before and after giving feeds?

options.D: 500 milliliters

question: What is an inter-referral pathway in healthcare?

options.A: A list of pharmacy prices for essential drugs in the market
options.B: A route taken by ambulance drivers to avoid heavy traffic congestion
options.C: A schedule for nursing shift change handovers on the ward
options.D: A structured system for moving patients between different levels of care

explanation: An inter-referral pathway is just a smooth roadmap for transferring a patient from a smaller clinic up to a bigger hospital when they need more specialized help. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of using BMI when assessing a very muscular athlete?

options.C: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to calculate accurately
options.D: It only applies to children and cannot be used for adults

question: Why do health interventions often collapse after external funding stops?

options.B: The community never truly felt ownership of the project

options.D: The national government banned all foreign medical supplies

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a patient has a respiratory diphtheria infection?

question: How do rapid diagnostic tests help in the fight against antibiotic resistance?

options.C: By killing all resistant bacteria instantly on contact
options.D: By distinguishing viral infections from bacterial ones

question: What is the primary overarching goal of Nigeria's National Population Policy?

options.D: Improving the standard of living and quality of life for citizens

question: Which set of symptoms points strongly to acute chest syndrome in a hospital patient?

question: What common operational problem often strains the relationship between Nigerian hospitals and HMOs?

options.C: Hospitals refusing to admit any patients who have insurance

question: How does evaluation differ from routine monitoring in health programmes?

question: Which of these is an early warning sign that conflict is brewing on a ward?
