options.B: Staff members starting a shared book club
options.C: An increase in overall patient satisfaction scores
options.D: Passive-aggressive notes and increased sarcasm during handovers

explanation: Sarcasm, eye-rolling, and sticky notes left behind are classic signs that team members are starting to rub each other the wrong way. [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h6)

question: What usually causes a Bartholin duct cyst to form?

options.A: Hormonal overproduction by the adrenal cortex
options.B: Blockage of the gland duct causing fluid to back up
options.C: Direct bacterial invasion from the urinary bladder
options.D: A genetic absence of the external genitalia glands

explanation: When the tiny tube (duct) leading from the Bartholin gland gets blocked, the fluid has nowhere to go and builds up into a cyst. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h2)

question: What is the medical term for a testicle that fails to move down into the scrotum?

options.A: Cryptorchidism
options.B: Hypospadias
options.C: Phimosis
options.D: Hydrocele

explanation: Cryptorchidism simply means the testicle didn't make the normal journey down into the scrotum before birth. You are doing great mastering these terms! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h4)

question: A patient recovering from a severe stroke struggles to walk and needs help rebuilding muscle strength. Which team member should be consulted?

options.A: Physician
options.B: Physiotherapist
options.C: Pharmacist
options.D: Social worker

explanation: You nailed it! Physiotherapists are experts at helping patients regain movement, strength, and independence after major setbacks like strokes. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h3)

question: What is a great way to improve vaccine turnout in a hesitant rural community?

options.A: Stopping all outreach visits and waiting for parents to find the clinic
options.B: Collaborating with respected local leaders and traditional rulers for health talks
options.C: Threatening parents with police arrest if they miss clinic appointments
options.D: Hiding the vaccine vials so people do not know what is being injected

explanation: Spot on! Traditional and community leaders have great influence and can help clear up rumors so families feel safe bringing their children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h7)

question: Why must a working defibrillator be kept close by during an EPS?

options.A: Dangerous heart rhythms are purposely triggered during the test
options.B: Sedation medications frequently cause permanent heart stoppage
options.C: The equipment is required to warm up the contrast dye
options.D: All patients suffer sudden cardiac arrest during catheter insertion

explanation: Because the doctors intentionally spark those weird rhythms to study them, the team must always be ready with a defibrillator just in case the heart needs help getting back to normal. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h4)

question: Which health benefit comes directly from regular physical education in schools?

options.A: Prevention of childhood obesity and improved motor skills
options.B: Immediate cure for congenital heart defects
options.C: Permanent enhancement of visual acuity
options.D: Complete elimination of infectious respiratory diseases

explanation: Correct! Staying active helps kids burn energy, build strong bones and muscles, and improve their coordination. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is health economics mostly about in a healthcare system?

options.A: How to eliminate all costs for patients seeking care
options.B: How to distribute equal salaries to all healthcare workers
options.C: How limited resources are used to provide health services
options.D: How to maximize profits for private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Think of health economics as managing limited funds and supplies so we can care for as many patients as possible. You've got this! [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h1)

question: What major public health threat is directly worsened by the over-prescription of antibiotics?

options.A: High blood pressure rates
options.B: Chronic kidney stone disease
options.C: Antimicrobial resistance
options.D: Nutritional vitamin deficiencies

explanation: Unnecessary antibiotic use teaches bacteria how to survive drug treatments, creating resistant strains that are hard to cure. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: What does the term 'plethora' mean in a patient with polycythaemia?

options.A: Severe swelling in the lower legs
options.B: A ruddy, reddish skin complexion
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the eyes
options.D: A sudden drop in blood pressure

explanation: Plethora just describes that classic red or flushed face look because there are so many blood cells packed near the skin surface. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T8#GNS311_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why is it important to report near-misses even though no patient was actually harmed?

options.A: To give the nursing supervisor extra paperwork to file away
options.B: To punish the staff member who almost made the mistake
options.C: To help identify hidden system weaknesses before a real injury happens
options.D: To increase the financial billing charges for the patient

explanation: Analyzing near-misses uncovers dangerous process flaws, allowing the hospital to fix them before a patient suffers actual harm. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h8)

question: You are teaching a client with heart failure how to avoid fluid buildup at home. What is the best advice to give?

options.A: Go to the emergency room every time you feel slightly tired
options.B: Stop taking your water pills whenever you feel thirsty
options.C: Drink extra water throughout the day to flush out toxins
options.D: Weigh yourself every morning at the same time and report sudden gains

explanation: You nailed it! Daily morning weights are a quick and reliable way to spot early fluid retention before it becomes dangerous. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h4)

question: A patient with a new leg cast complains of severe, throbbing pain that pain meds aren't helping. What is your first step?

options.A: Apply a heating pad over the cast to relax the cramped calf muscles
options.B: Administer a stronger dose of narcotic pain medication immediately
options.C: Elevate the leg above heart level and wait another two hours to see
options.D: Perform a neurovascular assessment of the toes and check for cast tightness

explanation: Unrelieved pain is a big red flag for dangerous swelling! Always check circulation, motion, and sensation (neurovascular check) right away. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h5)

question: In nutrition, what does the acronym RDA stand for?

options.A: Required Daily Amount
options.B: Regulated Diet Acid
options.C: Recommended Dietary Allowance
options.D: Rapid Daily Assessment

explanation: RDA stands for Recommended Dietary Allowance—the daily intake level that keeps nearly all healthy people thriving. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h3)

question: What was the main problem in drug markets before the WHO introduced essential drug guidelines?

options.A: Patients refused to take any form of modern medical treatment
options.B: There were absolute shortages of chemical factories globally
options.C: Governments completely banned the importation of foreign drugs
options.D: Markets were flooded with too many unverified and expensive drug formulations

explanation: Well done! Back then, the market was chaotic with countless pricey products of doubtful quality, which confused doctors and drained wallets. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main reason we use injection safety supplies in the hospital?

options.A: To make hospital storage rooms look neat and organized
options.B: To protect patients and nurses from blood-borne infections
options.C: To reduce the cost of buying drugs
options.D: To speed up intravenous fluid administration

explanation: You got this! Injection safety items like proper syringes and safety boxes are specifically designed to stop infections like HIV and hepatitis from spreading during procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is a major challenge nurses often face when providing palliative care in resource-limited settings?

options.A: An excess of high-tech equipment that overwhelms patients
options.B: Limited access to essential pain medications and specialized facilities
options.C: A complete absence of family involvement in patient care
options.D: Patients refusing all forms of basic nursing assessment

explanation: In many resource-constrained settings, getting a steady supply of pain relief like opioids can be tough. Nigerian nurses often have to be creative and strong advocates for their patients! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h8)

question: A patient scheduled for a skin snip is very anxious about pain. What is your best first response?

options.A: Cancel the procedure immediately without consulting the doctor
options.B: Administer general anesthesia to keep the patient completely asleep
options.C: Explain the procedure steps and reassure them about local anesthetic use
options.D: Tell the patient that the procedure is entirely painless and quick

explanation: Great nursing judgement! Walking patients through the steps and letting them know local numbing will be used calms their nerves. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h2)

question: A nurse refuses extra training because she believes management never promotes anyone fairly anyway. Which part of Vroom's theory is broken here?

options.A: Expectancy
options.B: Physiological need
options.C: Valence
options.D: Instrumentality

explanation: Instrumentality is your belief that good performance will actually lead to the promised reward. If you feel the system is rigged, that link is broken. [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h3)

question: Is there ever a time when a nurse can break patient confidentiality?

options.A: When the nurse wants to gossip with friends
options.B: When a coworker is simply curious about the diagnosis
options.C: When the patient misses three clinic appointments
options.D: When there is a risk of severe self-harm or abuse

explanation: Patient safety always comes first. If someone is in danger of hurting themselves or others, keeping them safe overrides privacy rules. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h3)

question: What usually happens to a new clinical project after the initial special attention and funding go away?

options.A: Performance often slips back to old habits
options.B: Staff automatically continue the practice forever
options.C: The hospital board shuts down the entire unit
options.D: Patient satisfaction drops to zero immediately

explanation: Without active efforts to sustain change, wards frequently slide back into their previous routines once the novelty and extra support fade. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which airway maneuver is safest to use when a neck injury is suspected?

options.A: Neck-hyperextension method
options.B: Rapid lateral neck rotation
options.C: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.D: Head-tilt/chin-lift maneuver

explanation: The jaw-thrust maneuver opens the airway without moving or bending the cervical spine, protecting the patient from further spinal cord damage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h3)

question: Why should newly hired nurses be introduced to the hospital's cultural values during orientation?

options.A: To discourage them from asking senior staff members for clinical help
options.B: To ensure they adopt expected behaviours and maintain the positive environment
options.C: To test their ability to memorize complex hospital administration bylaws
options.D: To reduce the amount of orientation salary the hospital has to pay them

explanation: Spot on! Early orientation helps new nurses fit right into the positive workplace culture, keeping standards of teamwork and safety high. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is the natural reservoir and host for Salmonella Typhi?

options.A: Humans
options.B: Aquatic fish
options.C: Rodents
options.D: Domestic livestock

explanation: Well done! Humans are the main host for Salmonella Typhi, meaning the infection cycle passes from person to person. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h2)

question: Why shouldn't incident reporting be treated like a disciplinary tool?

options.A: Only senior medical doctors have the authority to discipline staff
options.B: Fear of punishment makes staff hide mistakes, keeping dangers hidden
options.C: Disciplinary actions take too much time away from direct patient care
options.D: Hospital boards legally forbid managers from disciplining reporting nurses

explanation: You got it! If nurses are scared of being punished, they will hide their mistakes. We need honesty to make our wards safer. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h1)

question: What characterizes common cause variation in a healthcare process?

options.A: It is an unusual event that rarely happens
options.B: It is caused by a sudden equipment breakdown
options.C: It is natural and predictable variation
options.D: It shows an immediate breakthrough in care

explanation: Common cause variation is the normal, expected background noise of a stable daily process. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h4)

question: A ward manager wants to change wound care based on one small, poorly designed study. What should the staff nurse do first?

options.A: Critique the study to see if the methods support the new practice
options.B: Report the journal publisher to the nursing council
options.C: Immediately adopt the new method without reading the paper
options.D: Refuse to do any wound care for the patients

explanation: Before changing clinical routines, nurses should examine the strength and validity of the underlying research. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient shows you a skin mole that has recently changed color and grown irregularly. What should you do first?

options.A: Refer the patient for a prompt medical evaluation and biopsy.
options.B: Advise the patient to monitor the mole at home for another year.
options.C: Apply a medicated topical steroid cream to mole.
options.D: Reassure the patient that changing moles are always benign.

explanation: Any changing mole or spot needs a professional check-up right away to rule out skin cancer. You are learning to protect your patients! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h4)

question: Why can a non-cancerous (benign) heart tumour still be dangerous?

options.A: Its location inside the heart can block blood flow and cause dangerous blockages
options.B: It destroys all the red blood cells passing through the heart
options.C: Benign heart tumours automatically spread to the lungs and liver
options.D: Benign tumours always turn into aggressive cancers over time

explanation: Even though benign tumours aren't cancer, location is everything! Being stuck inside a vital organ means they can physically block blood flow or cause clots. You're doing brilliantly. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h2)

question: How does community participation influence the success of a primary health care program?

options.A: It ensures the community accepts and sustains the health interventions
options.B: It guarantees that every resident becomes a trained community health worker
options.C: It removes the need for government funding of local health posts
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all administrative duties to villagers

explanation: When people help plan their own health programs, they take ownership and support them long-term. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which level of government is mainly responsible for funding general hospitals that provide secondary care?

options.A: Local government council
options.B: International donor agencies
options.C: Private voluntary organizations
options.D: State government

explanation: Great job! State ministries of health take charge of managing and funding general hospitals, which make up our secondary care tier. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is it important to encourage a labouring mum to empty her bladder regularly?

options.A: To speed up cervical dilation past 10 centimeters
options.B: To stop Braxton Hicks contractions from returning
options.C: To prevent the bladder from obstructing fetal descent
options.D: To collect urine for a daily routine glucose test

explanation: Brilliant! A full bladder gets in the way like a water balloon in the pelvis, which can slow down the baby's journey down the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h4)

question: What is the main job of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) in the lab?

options.A: To grow fastidious bacteria on solid blood agar plates
options.B: To make many copies of tiny amounts of microbial DNA so they are easy to spot
options.C: To physically stain cell walls purple under a light microscope
options.D: To measure the patient's antibody response to a viral infection

explanation: Spot on! PCR is like a genetic photocopier that makes millions of copies of a germ's DNA so we can find even tiny traces. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h7)

question: What is the correct temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.A: Plus 15 degrees Celsius to plus 25 degrees Celsius
options.B: Minus 2 degrees Celsius to zero degrees Celsius
options.C: Plus 2 degrees Celsius to plus 8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Minus 15 degrees Celsius to minus 25 degrees Celsius

explanation: Keep this safe range in mind! +2°C to +8°C keeps most routine refrigerated vaccines cool and happy without freezing them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h4)

question: Why does early teenage pregnancy often negatively impact a young person's future?

options.A: It directly impairs cognitive functioning and memory
options.B: It automatically causes permanent physical disability in all young mothers
options.C: It frequently interrupts their education and limits economic opportunities
options.D: It permanently removes all support from their extended families

explanation: Parenthood during adolescence often forces teenagers to drop out of school, making it much harder to gain the skills needed for stable employment later in life. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is a major goal of public awareness campaigns in disaster management?

options.A: To sell emergency preparedness gear to private businesses
options.B: To replace formal emergency services with untrained citizens
options.C: To collect data for national census and population records
options.D: To educate citizens on evacuation routes and local hazard risks

explanation: When people know what signs to look out for and where to run for safety, they can protect themselves long before help arrives. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h6)

question: Which of the following is a suitable health topic for discussion at a PTA meeting?

options.A: Malaria prevention and insecticide-treated nets
options.B: Commercial transport licensing procedures
options.C: How to write university entrance examinations
options.D: The stock market price of agricultural goods

explanation: Malaria prevention is a critical public health topic that directly affects school attendance and student well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why do clinical instructors use structured grading tools instead of just going with their personal feelings?

options.A: To ensure students never fail a clinical placement.
options.B: To eliminate the need for written examinations entirely.
options.C: To reduce the total amount of time spent grading students.
options.D: To reduce personal bias and ensure fair, objective grading.

explanation: Structured tools keep grading fair and consistent for everyone, so your grade depends on your skills, not the instructor's mood. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: What causes stretch marks, or striae gravidarum, during pregnancy?

options.A: Fungal infections growing under tight clothing
options.B: Blockage of sweat glands by high hormone levels
options.C: Accumulation of excess subcutaneous fat deposits
options.D: Breaking of elastic fibers in the dermis from rapid stretching

explanation: As the belly grows quickly, the elastic fibers in the deeper skin layer stretch and tiny breaks happen, leading to stretch marks. Completely normal! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h3)

question: An unconscious child with cerebral malaria is brought into the emergency ward. What is your very first nursing priority?

options.A: Ensuring a clear airway and monitoring breathing
options.B: Discharging the patient home with anti-malarial tablets
options.C: Encouraging the mother to feed the child oral porridge
options.D: Checking visual acuity using a Snellen eye chart

explanation: Spot on! ABCs come first in nursing. An unconscious child can easily choke or struggle to breathe, so keeping that airway open is priority number one. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which of these situations is considered an intentional injury?

options.A: A youth falls off a moving commercial motorcycle and fractures a leg
options.B: A teenager gets stabbed during a street fight over money
options.C: A student drinks contaminated water and develops severe gastroenteritis
options.D: An adolescent accidentally touches a hot cooking stove and gets burned

explanation: Exactly! Assaults and physical fights are classed as intentional injuries because there is a deliberate human action meant to cause harm. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h2)

question: What practical method do community health nurses use while moving through a neighborhood to observe living conditions?

options.A: Surgical audit
options.B: Windshield survey
options.C: Biopsy screening
options.D: Laboratory blood analysis

explanation: Correct! A windshield survey is an observational method where the nurse travels through a community to spot living conditions and local resources. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a main job of the gonads?

options.A: Quickly fixing sudden drops in blood pressure
options.B: Supporting secondary sex traits like body hair
options.C: Helping with reproductive growth
options.D: Producing sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone

explanation: Spot on! Gonads focus on reproductive hormones. Blood pressure is managed by other organs like your kidneys and heart. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h6)

question: If the local currency drops in value, making imported drugs much more expensive, what should the DRF committee do?

options.A: Keep selling remaining stock at old prices until everything is completely gone
options.B: Borrow money from patients to pay for the next batch of imported drugs
options.C: Adjust selling prices based on current replacement costs to protect the fund
options.D: Stop selling medications entirely and wait for inflation to reverse itself naturally

explanation: If you don't adjust prices during currency drops, your sales revenue won't be enough to buy the next batch of drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the minimum recommended physical distance between residents in shared quarantine facilities?

options.A: No distance restriction is needed
options.B: One arm length or less
options.C: Exactly fifty centimeters
options.D: At least two meters

explanation: Maintaining a distance of two meters helps prevent the spread of respiratory droplets between individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h5)

question: What are the tiny calcium crystals in the utricle and saccule called?

options.A: Ampullae
options.B: Cupulas
options.C: Otoliths
options.D: Maculae

explanation: Otoliths are like tiny microscopic stones that add weight so gravity can pull on the jelly layer and help us feel motion. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a correct infection control step when nursing a patient with active TB?

options.A: Ensuring nurses wear fitted N95 respirator masks
options.B: Placing the patient in an airborne infection isolation room
options.C: Instructing the patient to cover their mouth when coughing
options.D: Keeping the patient's room doors and windows tightly sealed shut from fresh air

explanation: Sealing a room shut traps the infectious germs inside! We always need good ventilation or negative pressure to clear out the air safely. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the main goal of using a qualitative approach in a nursing study?

options.A: To find the exact percentage of patients cured by a drug
options.B: To measure the physical strength recovery of post-op clients
options.C: To gain a deep understanding of lived human experiences
options.D: To prove a mathematical relationship between two variables

explanation: Qualitative research helps us walk in our patients' shoes and truly understand what they are going through emotionally. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h3)

question: How do sudden altitude changes during an air medical evacuation affect a patient?

options.A: They instantly lower the patient's core body temperature
options.B: They prevent intravenous pumps from delivering fluids
options.C: They completely eliminate the risk of internal bleeding
options.D: They cause trapped gases inside body cavities to expand

explanation: As the plane climbs and air pressure drops, any trapped air inside the body—like in the gut or middle ear—expands just like a bag of chips at high altitude! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h4)

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: Distributing medical supplies to rural clinics
options.B: Diagnosing rare tropical infectious diseases
options.C: Writing detailed hospital administration reports
options.D: Promoting positive and sustainable health habits

explanation: You've got this! BCC is all about using interactive ways to help people and communities build healthy habits that actually last. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h1)

question: Which condition is a common indication for a musculoskeletal CT scan?

options.A: Acute muscle strains
options.B: Superficial skin lacerations
options.C: Complex bone fractures
options.D: Simple ligament sprains

explanation: CT scans are especially helpful for viewing complicated, multi-part fractures and seeing how bone fragments line up within a joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which implanted device is an absolute contraindication for an MRI scan?

options.A: Permanent dental fillings
options.B: Titanium total hip replacements
options.C: Certain older cardiac pacemakers
options.D: Plastic heart valve repairs

explanation: The strong magnet can interfere with the electrical wiring of older pacemakers, making them dangerous for the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h4)

question: When does a human baby first start picking up their normal body flora?

options.A: When solid foods are introduced
options.B: During the birth process
options.C: When the first adult teeth erupt
options.D: At puberty and hormonal shifts

explanation: Life's first big microbial exposure happens right at birth as the baby encounters microbes from the mother and the surrounding environment. Amazing how nature works! [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the best and most accurate lab test used to confirm chlamydia and gonorrhea infections of the cervix?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Basic metabolic serum panel
options.C: Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)
options.D: Complete blood count with differential

explanation: NAAT is the gold-standard test because it is super sensitive at picking up bacterial DNA from a simple swab or urine sample. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h5)

question: What is considered the most reliable indicator of a patient's pain intensity?

options.A: The nurse's clinical observation of vital signs
options.B: The physical size and depth of the tissue injury
options.C: The family member's estimate of the discomfort
options.D: The patient's personal self-report

explanation: Pain is a subjective experience, making the direct word of the patient the single most reliable source of information. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h3)

question: A patient is healing from major surgery. Which nutrient should you make sure they get more of to help their tissues repair?

options.A: Protein
options.B: Simple sugars
options.C: Saturated fats
options.D: Fiber

explanation: Spot on! Protein acts as the building blocks needed to fix cells, fight off infection, and rebuild damaged skin and muscles. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h2)

question: What is another common medical name for cervical erosion?

options.A: Cervical carcinoma
options.B: Cervical ectropion
options.C: Cervical dysplasia
options.D: Cervical stenosis

explanation: You will often hear cervical erosion called cervical ectropion in the clinic. It just means the inner cells of the cervix have moved outward a bit. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of indirect gender discrimination in a community?

options.A: Refusing to treat a patient based on their sex
options.B: A sign on a clinic door stating men cannot enter
options.C: Paying female nurses less than male nurses for the same job
options.D: Clinic hours that conflict with domestic caregiving duties

explanation: Indirect discrimination happens when a rule looks fair to everyone on paper, but actually makes it hard for one specific group to get care. You are building strong community nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h3)

question: Which physical sign is a reliable indicator that vital organs are getting enough blood flow?

options.A: Dry and cracked lips
options.B: Adequate urine output
options.C: Slow and deep breathing
options.D: Cold and pale fingers

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Good urine output tells you the kidneys are well-perfused, meaning the heart and blood vessels are keeping good pressure up. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is another common name for infectious conjunctivitis?

options.A: Lazy eye
options.B: Crossed eyes
options.C: Night blindness
options.D: Pink eye

explanation: Conjunctivitis is widely called pink eye because the small blood vessels in the conjunctiva become swollen and irritated, giving the eye a pink or red appearance. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h3)

question: How do osmotic purgatives work inside the gut?

options.A: Coating the intestinal lining with a thick oily film
options.B: Directly irritating the nerve endings inside the colon wall
options.C: Drawing water into the bowel lumen through high osmotic pressure
options.D: Swelling up with water to stretch the muscle fibers of the colon

question: Why does the stomach have very few microbes compared to the large intestine?

options.A: Enzymes in saliva destroy microbes before they enter
options.B: Strong gastric acids destroy most incoming microbes
options.C: Constant movement prevents microbes from attaching
options.D: The stomach wall lacks the nutrients bacteria require

explanation: Think about how acidic the stomach is! That strong acid acts like a chemical shield, destroying most of the microbes that try to pass through. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h3)

question: A hormone travels through the whole body, but why does it only affect certain cells?

options.A: Non-target cells actively destroy the hormone on contact
options.B: The blood only carries the hormone toward specific organs
options.C: Target cells are the only ones physically close to endocrine glands
options.D: Target cells possess specific receptors that bind to that hormone

explanation: Hormones are like keys floating around, but they only fit into matching locks (receptors) on their specific target cells. Neat, right? [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h1)

question: In which layer of the uterus does uterine cancer most commonly start?

options.A: Myometrium
options.B: Perimetrium
options.C: Cervical stroma
options.D: Endometrium

explanation: Spot on! The endometrium is the inner lining of the uterus, and that is where most uterine cancers begin. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T23#GNS216_U5_T23_h1)

question: A patient comes to your clinic with severe watery diarrhea and dehydration after drinking untreated stream water. What condition should you suspect?

options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

question: Why is it so important to include informal sector workers in Nigerian health insurance schemes?

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable and quiet voices are heard during community health projects?

options.B: Profit
options.C: Isolation
options.D: Speed

question: Why can severe blood loss lead to kidney failure?

options.A: The kidneys are overworked by trying to make more blood
options.B: Excess intravenous fluids drown kidney tissue
options.C: Low blood pressure reduces blood flow to the kidneys
options.D: Clotting factors block the urinary tubes completely

question: Why should community nurses use simple everyday language and live demonstrations during health talks?

options.C: To make the teaching session take as little time as possible
options.D: To hide complex medical terminology from uneducated citizens

question: Which part of the brain is the main control center for the fear response?

options.A: Occipital lobe

options.C: Amygdala
options.D: Medulla oblongata

question: What is the specific name of the stress ulcer that forms in the stomach due to severe burn trauma?

options.D: Curling's ulcer

question: What is the danger of using harsh chemical disinfectants on vaccine storage containers without proper rinsing?
